title: Remittance dependence, support for taxation and quality of public services in Africa
summary: The paper asks whether depending on remittances weakens citizens' support for taxation in Africa. For about two-thirds of citizens there is no significant effect, but for the remaining third remittance dependence significantly reduces support for taxation.
keyFindings: For the majority of citizens, remittance dependence has no significant effect on support for taxation.
For about one-third of citizens, remittance dependence significantly reduces support for taxation.
Citizens who rate public services positively are less likely to be in that group, so efficient public services may offset the effect.
methods: Afrobarometer round 7 data for about 45,000 respondents in 34 African countries, using a finite multilevel mixture of regressions.
